problem: Prior probabilistic-graph language grounding methods work for manipulation but scale poorly to navigation's large configuration space, and they rely on predefined object locations, so they cannot handle constraints on moving or currently unobserved objects (e.g. people).
motivation: Robots in changing environments must follow instructions like 'go to the restaurant and keep away from people', which contain both a goal and trajectory constraints. Constraint objects may be occluded, out of sensor range, or moving, so grounding must happen dynamically during navigation. Using a costmap motion planner as an intermediate layer avoids grounding directly to low-level actions.
key_idea: Classify instruction phrases into goal, constraint and uninformative with an attention Bi-LSTM, ground goals in a semantic map and constraints online via Mask R-CNN and Word2Vec similarity, and feed them into a costmap planner with an RL local collision-avoidance policy.
insight: A costmap works as a bridge between language and control: constraints become inflated obstacle regions that are added whenever the object is detected, so the trajectory changes accordingly (real-world with/without 'keep away from people' comparison). Attention and bidirectionality help phrase classification (Table: LSTM 82%, Bi-LSTM 88%, Att-Bi-LSTM 96%). Only qualitative navigation results are given, so end-to-end navigation benefit is not quantified.
method: Pre-processing: splits the instruction into phrases at conjunctions and commas.

Phrase classification: embedding, Bi-LSTM (forward and backward states summed), location-based attention (alpha_i = w^T tanh(h_i), softmax) and a 3-way softmax output for goal / constraint / uninformative.
Goal grounding: extracts the noun from the goal phrase, computes Word2Vec cosine similarity with semantic-map location names, and uses the 2D coordinate of the most similar one as the goal.

Dynamic constraint grounding: Mask R-CNN (COCO, 80 classes) instance segmentation; masked mean depth gives each object's 3D position in the robot frame; if Word2Vec similarity between the constraint noun and a detected label exceeds a threshold, the constraint is added.
Global planning: RRT on the SLAM-built semantic grid map (Cartographer localization) from the current position to the grounded goal.

Local planning: costmap holds static obstacles plus circular constraint regions (radius a) with smooth inflation; an intermediate waypoint from the global path is chosen and A* plans over the costmap.

Dynamic obstacle avoidance: a PPO-trained RL local collision-avoidance policy (4-hidden-layer network with laser scan, velocity and waypoint inputs, from Long et al. 2017) tracks the waypoints and avoids unmodeled obstacles.

setting.backbone: Att-Bi-LSTM phrase classifier (trained), Word2Vec (pretrained), Mask R-CNN (COCO-pretrained), RL collision-avoidance policy (PPO); classical RRT/A* planners
setting.training_data: Phrase classifier trained on a self-collected dataset of 500 navigation instructions (tested on 300 phrases); Word2Vec on Wikipedia corpus; Mask R-CNN on COCO; RL policy from prior work, trained in multi-agent scenarios
setting.observation: RGB-D camera, laser scan, 2D localization in a prebuilt semantic map
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands from the local collision-avoidance policy following A*/RRT waypoints
setting.simulator: custom simulated scene with static obstacles and pedestrians (unspecified simulator); Turtlebot in the real world
setting.privileged: predefined SLAM-built global map, manually annotated with semantic location names; accurate localization assumed

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; only phrase-classification accuracy (LSTM 82%, Bi-LSTM 88%, Att-Bi-LSTM 96% on a 300-phrase custom test set) and path length/time versus number of constraints (2.83 m/5.3 s with 0 constraints to 3.52 m/7.6 s with 6) are reported.
results: Att-Bi-LSTM reaches 96% phrase-classification accuracy versus 88% for Bi-LSTM and 82% for LSTM. The system follows instructions successfully in a simulated scene with pedestrians and in two real-world Turtlebot scenes, and adding constraints lengthens path and time modestly (2.83 m/5.3 s to 3.52 m/7.6 s for 0 to 6 constraints). Evaluation is qualitative and there are no baseline navigation comparisons.
limitations: Evaluation is small and mostly qualitative (video demos), with no standard benchmark or baseline comparison of navigation success.
Relies on a prebuilt, manually annotated semantic map, a closed 80-class COCO detector and Word2Vec similarity thresholds, which limits open-vocabulary grounding and unseen environments.
Pipeline is modular, not end-to-end, and only supports a fixed set of instruction types (goal, constraints).
builds_on: Long et al. 2017 RL collision avoidance
